# requireRichTextValue

<link-summary>Returns the value as a rich text value, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireRichTextValue() — Returns the value as a rich text value, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireRichTextValue(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a RichTextValue object."
): GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.RichTextValue;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "RichTextValue"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                     | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                       | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a RichTextValue object."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.RichTextValue` — the same value, typed as a rich text value.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                           |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a rich text value. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const value = SpreadsheetApp.newRichTextValue().setText("a").build();

requireRichTextValue(value); // => value
requireRichTextValue({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireRichTextValue(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
